summary: Extracted the full Birmingham City Council pre-application submission evidence for 115 Vicarage Road, Kings Heath, B14 7QG. The pre-app (submitted 09/06/2026 via BCC "Apply for pre-application advice" online form, householder category) was made by agent Rouhel Ahmed on behalf of applicant/payee Mohammed Ahmed, fee £166.80 inc VAT, council submission reference 17123150. The verbatim advice request was: "Proposed double storey rear extension. Require confirmation of the size of the extension in relation to the 45 degree rule from neighbouring properties." Location plan confirms plot area 607.14 sq m, scales 1:1250 (location) and 1:500 (block), no written plot dimensions. Five site photos show the existing single-storey rear projection at no.115, the alleyway gap to no.113's rendered extension, and no.117's lean-to conservatory abutting the boundary. No evidence of a site-visit request appears in any screenshot provided.

facts.topic: Location plan — plot area and dimensions
facts.detail: The red-line plot is annotated '607.14m2' on both the 1:1250 location plan and 1:500 block plan. This is the ONLY written dimension/area on the sheet — no linear plot dimensions (width/depth) are written anywhere; any lengths would have to be scaled off the sheet using the 1:500/1:1250 scale bars.
facts.value: 607.14 sq m plot area (written); no linear dimensions written

facts.topic: Location plan — plot orientation and shape
facts.detail: Vicarage Road runs along the plot's frontage at the top of the plan (road labelled 'VICARAGE ROAD'); Colmore Road labelled curving along/near the side/rear-left. The red-line plot is a long, narrow, near-parallelogram strip running back from Vicarage Road at an angle (rear boundary skewed, not square to the frontage), with the house (labelled 115) sited at the front of the plot and a very long rear garden — the garden depth visually many times the house depth. North point is on the sheet (top-right notes panel) but the plan itself is not annotated with a north arrow adjacent to the maps; on the block plan Vicarage Road is top-left and the garden runs down-right. Judged against typical OS orientation the long garden runs roughly south-east from the road, but this is interpretation, not written on the drawing.
facts.value: Long narrow rear-garden plot off Vicarage Road, skewed rear boundary

facts.detail: Block plan (1:500) labels: '117' to the left (south-west side) of 115 — a larger, wider footprint building close to/at the shared boundary; '115' the subject semi with a small rear projection shown; '113' immediately to the right (north-east) with its own rear projection, and '111' beyond it. The footprints of 115 and 113 rear projections are drawn close together with a small gap (the alleyway) but no gap dimension is written. Rear-boundary properties: the rear of the plot backs onto land/gardens off Colmore Road (Colmore Road curves around the left/rear; a 'Scout Hut' labelled building and other Colmore Road plots appear beyond the side/rear on the 1:1250 plan). No rear-neighbour building is shown close to the shared rear boundary on the block plan extract.
facts.value: 117 SW side (attached semi pair), 113 NE side with adjacent rear projection, long garden backing towards Colmore Road land incl. Scout Hut area

facts.detail: Full-width rear view of 115 (right, painted render semi with hipped clay-tile roof) and 117 (left, attached semi): 115 has an existing flat-roof single-storey rear projection across most of its rear with a rear door, small side window, large kitchen window and a wide 4-leaf glazed door/screen set; two-storey rear wall above with first-floor windows. To the left, 117's white lean-to conservatory is visible behind the timber close-board boundary fence; to the right, the brick flank of 113 and its panel fence. Large overgrown paved patio and lawn in foreground; mature tree right of centre. No dimensions.

Looking up at no.113's two-storey brick rear/side wing from behind a fence: brick gable with first-floor window, ground-floor window pair, black rainwater goods; beyond it a white-rendered building with dark tiled roof and rooflight (appears to be the rear of 115's neighbour context / another property). Shows 113 already has a substantial two-storey rear element. No dimensions.
facts.value: No.113 two-storey brick rear wing photo
